name: Hand and Foot
description: Hand and Foot is a popular Canasta-style rummy game typically played by four players in partnerships. Each player receives two sets of cards: a 'hand' (played first) and a 'foot' (played after the hand is depleted). The objective is to form melds and canastas (7-card melds) while managing special cards like Red Threes (bonus) and Black Threes (penalty). Features 'books' (clean and dirty canastas), minimum meld requirements that increase each round, and strategic decisions about when to go out.

history.origins: Developed in the United States as a variant of Canasta, adding the unique 'hand and foot' mechanic where players manage two separate sets of cards.
timeline: 1940s: Canasta becomes popular in the USA.
1980s-1990s: Hand and Foot emerges as a Canasta variant.
Present: Popular in North America, especially in social and family settings.
history.cultural: A staple of North American card gaming, particularly popular in retirement communities and family gatherings.
history.evolution: Evolved from Canasta by adding the hand/foot mechanic, increasing the number of decks, and introducing stricter canasta requirements.

setup.players: 2-6 players. Best with 4 in partnerships (partners sit opposite).
setup.deck: 5-6 standard 52-card decks + Jokers (typically 5 decks for 4 players).
setup.dealing: Each player receives TWO sets of cards: Hand (11-15 cards) and Foot (11-15 cards face-down). Remaining cards form the stock. Top card turned face-up to start discard pile (if Red Three or Wild, bury it and turn another).
setup.equipment: Two denominations of chips or counters for scoring.

rules.objective: Score the most points over 4 rounds by forming melds and canastas. Be the first partnership to go out (empty hand and foot).
rules.gameplay: Turn Structure: 1. Draw: Draw 2 cards from stock OR pick up entire discard pile (if you can immediately use the top card in a meld). 2. Meld: Lay down melds or add to existing partnership melds. 3. Discard: Discard 1 card to end turn. Minimum Initial Meld: Round 1: 50 points, Round 2: 90 points, Round 3: 120 points, Round 4: 150 points. Picking Up Your Foot: After playing all cards from your hand, pick up your foot. If you discard your last hand card, pick up foot on next turn. If you play all hand cards without discarding, immediately pick up foot and continue playing.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; if not, may play any card.
Red Threes: +100 points if melded, -100 if caught in hand/foot.
Black Threes: Cannot be melded; -5 points if caught in hand/foot.
To go out: Need at least 1 clean and 1 dirty canasta; both partners must have picked up their feet.

strategy.basic: Focus on forming canastas quickly. Avoid getting stuck with Red Threes or Black Threes at the end.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate with your partner. If your partner is close to going out, help them by forming the required canastas.
strategy.advanced: Track which cards have been discarded to anticipate what's left in the stock. Time your 'going out' to maximize your score while minimizing opponents' scores.
tips: Red Threes are a double-edged sword: +100 if you go out, -100 if caught.
Black Threes are only useful for blocking the discard pileâ€”discard them when safe.
Clean canastas are worth more than dirty ones. Prioritize them.

scoring.description: Points for melds, canastas, cards in hand. Deductions for unmelded cards. Clean canastas worth 500, dirty canastas worth 300. Red Threes +100 if melded, -100 if caught. Game played over 4 rounds.
scoring.winCondition: Highest total score after 4 rounds wins. First partnership to 10,000+ points across multiple games wins the session.

synthesis.shortDescription: A partnership rummy variant where players develop two separate card holdings ('Hand' and 'Foot') to accumulate points through melds and canastas.
